description: Experience the unparalleled tang and chewy interior of a true San Francisco Sourdough Boule, a bread renowned for its rustic charm and distinct flavor profile. This iconic American loaf, with its perfectly golden, crackly crust, is a testament to the art of slow fermentation and traditional baking techniques. Enjoy a slice plain, toasted, or as the perfect accompaniment to any meal.

instructions.title: Prepare the Autolyse
instructions.text: In a large mixing bowl, combine the bread flour and 325 grams of warm water. Mix until no dry flour remains and a shaggy dough forms. Cover the bowl with a damp cloth or plastic wrap and let it rest for 30 minutes to 1 hour. This step, known as autolyse, helps the flour fully hydrate and gluten to begin developing.

instructions.title: Incorporate Starter and Salt
instructions.text: Add the active sourdough starter and salt to the autolysed dough. Pour the remaining 25 grams of warm water over the starter and salt. Mix thoroughly by hand, squeezing and folding the dough until the starter and salt are fully integrated and the dough feels more cohesive. This may take 5-10 minutes of gentle kneading.

instructions.title: Bulk Fermentation with Folds
instructions.text: Cover the bowl and let the dough rest for 30 minutes. Begin the bulk fermentation process, performing 4 sets of stretch and folds over the next 2-3 hours, with 30-minute intervals between each set. To perform a stretch and fold, wet your hand, grab a portion of the dough, stretch it upwards, and fold it over itself. Rotate the bowl and repeat until all sides have been folded. Cover and let the dough continue to ferment at room temperature (around 75F/24C) until it has increased in volume by about 30-50% and shows signs of activity (bubbles). This can take 4-6 hours depending on your starter and room temperature.

instructions.title: Pre-Shape and Bench Rest
instructions.text: Gently turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface. Using a dough scraper, gently shape the dough into a loose round or rectangle. Avoid deflating the dough too much. Cover the dough with a damp cloth and let it rest for 20-30 minutes. This bench rest allows the gluten to relax, making the final shaping easier.

instructions.title: Final Shape and Cold Proof
instructions.text: Lightly flour a banneton or a bowl lined with a floured linen cloth. Gently shape the dough into a tight boule, creating tension on the surface. Place the shaped dough seam-side up into the prepared banneton. Cover the banneton with plastic wrap or a shower cap and refrigerate for 12-18 hours. Cold proofing develops flavor and allows for easier scoring.

instructions.title: Bake the Boule
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 500F (260C) with a Dutch oven inside for at least 45 minutes. Carefully remove the hot Dutch oven. Gently invert the cold dough from the banneton into the hot Dutch oven. Score the top of the dough with a sharp razor blade or lame. Cover the Dutch oven and bake for 20 minutes. Reduce the oven temperature to 450F (230C), remove the lid, and continue baking for another 15-20 minutes, or until the crust is deeply golden brown and the internal temperature reaches 200-210F (93-99C). Let the boule cool completely on a wire rack for at least 1-2 hours before slicing.

tips: Ensure your sourdough starter is active and bubbly before you begin, as this is crucial for proper leavening and flavor development.
For the best crust and oven spring, always preheat your Dutch oven thoroughly. A super hot vessel creates steam, which is essential for a beautiful loaf.
Allow your baked boule to cool completely on a wire rack before slicing. Slicing too early can result in a gummy texture and compromises the crumb structure.
